messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A shelf of half-used labels and tape; then several items no longer have obvious homes. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "I tap the shelf once and leave the tape where it sits. I tap the label on the edge and tap the shelf once. I tap the tape twice and leave it there."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "the label says “old, bright, old smell.” i tap the tape with my thumb. the label says “new.” i put the old one on the shelf. the tape stays. i tap the shelf with the other one. the old one catches. i put the old one on the bench. the shelf stays. the label says “old, bright, old smell.” i leave the old one. the bench stays."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I put the labels back. One. Two. Three. I remove the tape. The labels are wrong. I write the wrong one on one corner. I put the tape back. I check the label under the cloth. No—the label is wrong. I leave it there. I keep the labels."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "\"One home. Likely.\" You lift the tape, but the labels are still there. \"One mark. Likely.\" You check the watch and leave the watch aside."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "I take one label. dirty. i rub it with my sleeve. “keep.” i leave the tape in the shelf. then i check the broken gear. no. i put the label back and pocket the tape. maybe the order matters."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i tap the tape once, but the label says, \"no,\" so i copy the last sentence on one corner. i put the label back in the shelf, but leave the tape untouched. the labels keep showing, but i don’t touch them."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i tap the shelf. i tap the tape. i put the label on the shelf. i leave the tape on the shelf. i put the label back on the shelf."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "I pull one label out and put it in my pocket. “I put it in the shelf. then I look at the others. no one has it yet.” i leave the tape in the shelf, but i do not touch it. the label stays on the shelf, waiting for the next one to come along."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "I tap the tape with a pencil until it slips. The label sticks, and I mark the spot with ‘no home.’ My log says ‘tape,’ then ‘no home.’ I lean toward the tape because it feels more durable. ‘I mark the label with the tape because that is what it looks like.’"}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i tap the tape once, tapping the label edge twice. “one,” i say, then tap the shelf edge twice with my fingertip. “the tape keeps moving, so i write the label upside down.” i copy the label on the scrap beside it."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i tap the tape once with my fingernail, then leave the labels where they are. i keep the items in a drawer for later."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "i leave the half-used labels aside and tap the shelf again with a pencil mark. if the tape still sticks, i leave the label intact and mark the new spot with a pencil jerk. if it stays, i leave the old label beside the new one and show the difference."}]
